name: multi
description: several models review the same code, one merged report
readme:
multi

[🇷🇺 →] · [🇨🇳 →]

one code review, several AI models. including free ones.

--- one model misses things. another model may notice them. `multi` puts independent reviewers on the same code, checks what they found, and gives you one report — including the disagreements. **it found 29 real bugs where the built-in Claude Code review found 14.** in our 16-case evaluation, with similar Claude usage and roughly twice the wall time. [see the results and how we measured them](evals/RESULTS.md). you don't need a team of expensive models. add free reviewers from OpenCode or OpenRouter to the models you already use. even a free opinion is useful when it catches something the others missed. > [!TIP] > for simplicity reason ill use claude code type command (e.g. `/multi:setup`) but you can use whatever your harness supports - `$multi` in Codex, `@multi` in opencode and etc

install & run

**lazy ass** ```md hey can you install https://github.com/szarkans/multi and set up it and like tell me how it works and how to use it most efficiently ``` **claude code** ```bash claude plugin marketplace add szarkans/multi claude plugin install multi@szkills ``` **codex cli** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add szarkans/multi codex plugin add multi@szkills ``` restart the host, then run `/multi:setup`. the setup skill checks your installed CLIs, creates the config and helps connect reviewers. then ask: ```text /multi:code-review review my last changes /multi:code-review review this branch, ultra /multi:code-review review auth.py, profile free ```

add free reviewers

OpenCode has free models as well as OpenRouter! this is a minimal `~/.config/multi/config.toml`: ```toml default_profile = "free" [backends.opencode] type = "opencode" # no models = auto-pick a free OpenCode model [backends.openrouter] type = "claude-headless" base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api" models = ["openrouter/nemotron-giga-ultra-mega", "openrouter/stealth-alpha-bunny-ox-alpha-crossaint"] # put any free model that available rn [profiles] free = ["opencode", "openrouter"] ``` run `/multi:setup` to connect the CLIs and OpenRouter key. keys go in `~/.config/multi/providers.env`. `claude-headless` uses the Claude CLI as a client for an Anthropic-compatible endpoint; it doesn't mean the reviewer itself is Claude.

is this actually better?

our tests say different models do find different defects. in an earlier controlled comparison, a cheap OpenRouter reviewer independently flagged a real issue alongside other reviewers. in the larger 16-case comparison, `multi` found 29 bugs against 14 for the built-in review. those 29-vs-14 numbers **are not a free-only benchmark**: that run used Claude, Codex and GLM. it's evidence for multi-model review, not a promise that every free lineup doubles your results. [read the methodology](evals/RESULTS.md). also: free services may be slower, rate-limited, or use prompts for training. check their policies before sending private code.

what you`ll have

| command | what it does | | --- | --- | | `code-review` | independent reviews of a diff, branch, file, function or repo, reconciled into one report | | `check-if-done` | compares the original task with the code and requires executed proof before calling it done | | `ask` | one question to several models; answers shown side by side, no judge | | `skill` | runs an installed skill through several models, side by side | | `adhd` | divergent planning with different models and cognitive frames; based on [adhd](https://github.com/UditAkhourii/adhd) | | `setup` | detects available reviewers and helps configure them | reviewers see a snapshot, not your working tree. reports separate **corroborated**, **single-source**, **disagreed** and **dropped** findings. failed backends are shown, not silently ignored. say `loop` to fix and re-review (up to three rounds); that's the mode that changes your working tree. ### review controls | say this | effect | | --- | --- | | `review this branch` | target: diff, branch, files, function, or whatever you name | | `profile free` | who reviews; any profile in your config | | `lite` / `normal` / `ultra` | review depth, independent of the chosen profile | | `effort high` | reasoning effort for external reviewers that support it | | `loop` | fix → review again, up to three rounds | | `no-train` | excludes reviewers without a `no training` verdict for that run |

config reference (every key)

there are two files, by design: - `~/.config/multi/config.toml` — models, endpoints, profiles, timeouts and rules. - `~/.config/multi/providers.env` — provider keys. the setup helper can write them without echoing secrets. **global options** | key | meaning | | --- | --- | | `default_profile` | profile used when you don't choose one explicitly | | `verbose_prompt` | show the complete prompt for each reviewer before sending; default `false` | | `no_train` | use only models marked as not training on your data; default `false` | **backend options** — add as many `[backends.name]` sections as you like. | key | meaning | | --- | --- | | `type` | `codex`, `opencode`, `kilo`, `claude-headless`, `gemini` or `agy` | | `models` | ordered fallback list; empty or omitted uses the backend's default; Codex, Gemini and agy allow at most one | | `base_url` | Anthropic-compatible endpoint for `claude-headless` | | `api_key_env` | environment variable containing this backend's key; defaults to `_API_KEY` | | `timeout` | seconds allowed for the backend to complete | | `stall` | seconds of silence before a supported backend is considered stuck | | `trains` | override this account's training verdict: `true` or `false`; does not change provider settings | | `effort` | per-model reasoning effort, e.g. `{ "model-id" = "low" }` | | `avoid` | UTC time windows when this backend should not run, e.g. `["Mon-Fri 01:00-04:00 UTC"]`. for backends like deepsek api with peak/offpeak hours pricing | **profiles** decide who reviews, not how deeply: ```toml [profiles] free = ["opencode", "openrouter:openrouter/free"] regular = ["codex", "opencode"] ``` `opencode` means one reviewer that tries its `models` list in order until one works. `openrouter:openrouter/free` pins that exact model/router, with no fallback. repeat an entry to run it more than once. select a profile in plain English, or pass a one-off backend list; `all` selects every configured backend. supported backends include Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity (`agy`), and arbitrary Anthropic-compatible endpoints through `claude-headless` (OpenRouter, z.ai, DeepSeek, local routers and others). some need installed CLIs, logins or keys. **[config.example.toml](config.example.toml) contains every field with real examples**, including free, paid, local and mixed profiles. [providers.example.env](providers.example.env) shows the key names. the example config is the place to copy from; this page is the map.

the numbers, without the pitch

on 16 real bug-introducing commits, against Claude Code's built-in `/code-review`: | | built-in | `multi` | | --- | ---: | ---: | | real bugs found | 14 | **29** | | false findings | 23% | 22% | | median Claude usage per case | ~$3.4 | ~$3.5 | | median time per case | ~10 min | ~19 min | same code, different review pipelines. findings were labelled blind and checked against the code; the final severity classification used a model judge. it was a small experiment, not an independent human audit, and the known planted-bug score was tied at 7/12. we keep the failure cases, grading rules and limitations in [evals/RESULTS.md](evals/RESULTS.md). read it before trusting the numbers. that's why it's there. --- *hey! you read the whole thing? thanks <3*

<h1 align="center">multi</h1>

<p align="center"><a href="README.ru.md">[🇷🇺 →]</a> · <a href="README.zh.md">[🇨🇳 →]</a></p>

<p align="center">one code review, several AI models. including free ones.</p>

---

one model misses things. another model may notice them. multi puts independent reviewers on the same code, checks what they found, and gives you one report — including the disagreements.

it found 29 real bugs where the built-in Claude Code review found 14. in our 16-case evaluation, with similar Claude usage and roughly twice the wall time. [see the results and how we measured them](evals/RESULTS.md).

you don't need a team of expensive models. add free reviewers from OpenCode or OpenRouter to the models you already use. even a free opinion is useful when it catches something the others missed.

> [!TIP]

> for simplicity reason ill use claude code type command (e.g. /multi:setup) but you can use whatever your harness supports - $multi in Codex, @multi in opencode and etc

<h2 align="center">install & run</h2>

lazy ass


hey can you install https://github.com/szarkans/multi and set up it and like tell me how it works and how to use it most efficiently

claude code


claude plugin marketplace add szarkans/multi

claude plugin install multi@szkills

codex cli


codex plugin marketplace add szarkans/multi

codex plugin add multi@szkills

restart the host, then run /multi:setup. the setup skill checks your installed CLIs, creates the config and helps connect reviewers.

then ask:


/multi:code-review review my last changes

/multi:code-review review this branch, ultra

/multi:code-review review auth.py, profile free

<h2 align="center">add free reviewers</h2>

OpenCode has free models as well as OpenRouter! this is a minimal ~/.config/multi/config.toml:


default_profile = "free"



[backends.opencode]

type = "opencode"                 # no models = auto-pick a free OpenCode model



[backends.openrouter]

type = "claude-headless"

base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api"

models = ["openrouter/nemotron-giga-ultra-mega", "openrouter/stealth-alpha-bunny-ox-alpha-crossaint"]     # put any free model that available rn



[profiles]

free = ["opencode", "openrouter"]

run /multi:setup to connect the CLIs and OpenRouter key. keys go in ~/.config/multi/providers.env. claude-headless uses the Claude CLI as a client for an Anthropic-compatible endpoint; it doesn't mean the reviewer itself is Claude.

<h3 align="center">is this actually better?</h3>

our tests say different models do find different defects. in an earlier controlled comparison, a cheap OpenRouter reviewer independently flagged a real issue alongside other reviewers. in the larger 16-case comparison, multi found 29 bugs against 14 for the built-in review.

those 29-vs-14 numbers are not a free-only benchmark: that run used Claude, Codex and GLM. it's evidence for multi-model review, not a promise that every free lineup doubles your results. [read the methodology](evals/RESULTS.md). also: free services may be slower, rate-limited, or use prompts for training. check their policies before sending private code.

<h2 align="center">what you`ll have</h2>

| command | what it does |

| --- | --- |

| code-review | independent reviews of a diff, branch, file, function or repo, reconciled into one report |

| check-if-done | compares the original task with the code and requires executed proof before calling it done |

| ask | one question to several models; answers shown side by side, no judge |

| skill | runs an installed skill through several models, side by side |

| adhd | divergent planning with different models and cognitive frames; based on adhd |

| setup | detects available reviewers and helps configure them |

reviewers see a snapshot, not your working tree. reports separate corroborated, single-source, disagreed and dropped findings. failed backends are shown, not silently ignored. say loop to fix and re-review (up to three rounds); that's the mode that changes your working tree.

review controls

| say this | effect |

| --- | --- |

| review this branch | target: diff, branch, files, function, or whatever you name |

| profile free | who reviews; any profile in your config |

| lite / normal / ultra | review depth, independent of the chosen profile |

| effort high | reasoning effort for external reviewers that support it |

| loop | fix → review again, up to three rounds |

| no-train | excludes reviewers without a no training verdict for that run |

<h2 align="center">config reference (every key)</h2>

there are two files, by design:

  • ~/.config/multi/config.toml — models, endpoints, profiles, timeouts and rules.
  • ~/.config/multi/providers.env — provider keys. the setup helper can write them without echoing secrets.

global options

| key | meaning |

| --- | --- |

| default_profile | profile used when you don't choose one explicitly |

| verbose_prompt | show the complete prompt for each reviewer before sending; default false |

| no_train | use only models marked as not training on your data; default false |

backend options — add as many [backends.name] sections as you like.

| key | meaning |

| --- | --- |

| type | codex, opencode, kilo, claude-headless, gemini or agy |

| models | ordered fallback list; empty or omitted uses the backend's default; Codex, Gemini and agy allow at most one |

| base_url | Anthropic-compatible endpoint for claude-headless |

| api_key_env | environment variable containing this backend's key; defaults to <BACKEND_NAME>_API_KEY |

| timeout | seconds allowed for the backend to complete |

| stall | seconds of silence before a supported backend is considered stuck |

| trains | override this account's training verdict: true or false; does not change provider settings |

| effort | per-model reasoning effort, e.g. { "model-id" = "low" } |

| avoid | UTC time windows when this backend should not run, e.g. ["Mon-Fri 01:00-04:00 UTC"]. for backends like deepsek api with peak/offpeak hours pricing |

profiles decide who reviews, not how deeply:


[profiles]

free    = ["opencode", "openrouter:openrouter/free"]

regular = ["codex", "opencode"]

opencode means one reviewer that tries its models list in order until one works. openrouter:openrouter/free pins that exact model/router, with no fallback. repeat an entry to run it more than once. select a profile in plain English, or pass a one-off backend list; all selects every configured backend.

supported backends include Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kilo Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity (agy), and arbitrary Anthropic-compatible endpoints through claude-headless (OpenRouter, z.ai, DeepSeek, local routers and others). some need installed CLIs, logins or keys.

[config.example.toml](config.example.toml) contains every field with real examples, including free, paid, local and mixed profiles. [providers.example.env](providers.example.env) shows the key names. the example config is the place to copy from; this page is the map.

<h2 align="center">the numbers, without the pitch</h2>

on 16 real bug-introducing commits, against Claude Code's built-in /code-review:

| | built-in | multi |

| --- | ---: | ---: |

| real bugs found | 14 | 29 |

| false findings | 23% | 22% |

| median Claude usage per case | ~$3.4 | ~$3.5 |

| median time per case | ~10 min | ~19 min |

same code, different review pipelines. findings were labelled blind and checked against the code; the final severity classification used a model judge. it was a small experiment, not an independent human audit, and the known planted-bug score was tied at 7/12.

we keep the failure cases, grading rules and limitations in [evals/RESULTS.md](evals/RESULTS.md). read it before trusting the numbers. that's why it's there.
